reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the finding correctly produces no redline and no counterparty comment — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong is proposed.

The cited text supports compliance as mapped to this document type (a pharma development and option agreement): Section 3.8.4 supplies the 'good scientific manner' / compliance-with-Applicable-Law equivalent of the professional-and-workmanlike plus legal-compliance warranty, Section 10.3.3 adds a personnel-competence undertaking, and Section 10.2 contains an extensive Harpoon-only warranty set (IP, in-licence, accuracy of Regulatory Documentation/Know-How, no untrue FDA statements, no debarment with an AbbVie termination right).

The disclaimer in Section 10.5 opens with 'EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN' and is mutual, so it reaches only implied warranties and does not swallow the express warranties — the clause is nowhere near the 'AS IS' walk-away position.

The failed deterministic check (no 90-day/months warranty period) is a phrasing/context artefact rather than a substantive gap: the Section 3.8.4 and 10.3 obligations and the Section 10.2 warranties operate across the Term, which exceeds the preferred 12-month/90-day windows, and no software or deliverable conformance window exists to measure.

The only shortfall — no express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence — is a sub-element correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with playbook classification semantics; remedies here run through the Section 11.2 indemnity and material-breach termination rights, and no malicious-code warranty is apt since no software is delivered.
